items.title: Review and merge PR #121
items.body:
One speed fix a player feels: the first piece picked up after a game’s entrance no longer waits seconds for the warm-up of the marks of play. Also: the warm-up in one frame, three correctness fixes (a computer that could stall for ever, a computer game that rewound after its storage filled, guessable game ids), and seven checks that could pass on broken code, or rules nothing enforced, now enforced. Against main, the primary rows run at ×1.061 (4 pairs, none called better or worse); the first pick 2.39 s → 475 ms on that code and 2.44 s → 812 ms on the final code (both called better). CI green on the PR (client, server-tests, e2e games/session/rest).

Like the last runs it bundles a server change (SystemRandom ids, one server test) and bench/lint changes with the client work; CLAUDE.md asks for one change per PR.

items.recommend: Squash-merge once CI is green. If you want the one-change rule applied strictly, I split out 26bae12 + 3016c9b (server) first.

items.title: Keep the first-pick fix? It moves the warm-up’s cost, it does not remove it
items.body: In software rendering the warm-up of the marks of play costs about 2 s of GPU time, and it lands on whatever the player does first after the entrance. On main that is the first pick (about 2.4 s). This branch links the programs under the entrance and reads them back once the board rests: the first pick drops to about 0.8 s, but the second and third picks and the computer’s second reply each wait about 0.3 s more. Net, the player waits about 0.8 s less over the first few actions; nothing is called worse on the final code (the computer’s reply +46% and selecting +41% lean worse, not called; an earlier version made the reply +114%, called, and was fixed). On a real GPU these links take milliseconds and none of this shows. No row times the entrance’s smoothness (T16).

items.title: Say so on screen when a computer game can no longer be saved?
items.body: Once a long computer game outgrows the browser’s storage, its moves are kept for this visit only (fixed this run: they no longer rewind). A reload loses them. Today the only sign is a console warning.
items.recommend: Yes, one short line in the HUD’s existing notice style (“This game can’t be saved here”). It is new interface copy, so it is your call (ledger R5).

items.title: The target is not met against the first recorded run
items.body: The target was the primary rows 1.2× faster than the first recorded run (92ce041). Measured today, final code against it, 3 pairs (92ce041 had no computer player, so those two rows are missing): ×0.893 (last run measured ×0.968 on its own code; the two runs’ VMs differ, so compare within a run only). Called better: a shared game’s page −44%, reopening a long game −31%. Called worse: joining’s first board frame 1.57 → 5.12 s (+216%), the opponent’s move landing 136 → 215 ms (+58%; against main this run it was −5.8%, not called, so it came in before this branch; it was +4.6% uncalled last run), the phone start page +7.4%. Still worse in the diagnostics: the first pick 33 ms → 764 ms (2.34 s last run), JS heap on a reopened 2,000-ply game +34%, one texture more after 16 plies (the garden copy, not a leak: X5a). The lobby, the garden, the preview and the entrance all came after 92ce041; the join remains the largest wait.

items.recommend: Next run, the join (J3): its 5.4 s is three.js reading uniforms back behind SwiftShader’s queue of lobby frames. That needs a design decision about how many lobby frames to draw while the game’s board links (below).

items.title: The join’s wait: fewer lobby frames while the board links? (design call)
items.body: A CPU profile of a join shows the joiner’s long tasks are getUniforms read-backs inside render(), each waiting for the GPU to finish the lobby frames queued before it (0.66, 1.15, 0.53 s), plus 0.3 s creating the board’s WebGL context. Linking ahead (tried, rejected) moves links, not those waits. What would shorten them is drawing fewer lobby frames while the board’s canvas starts: the arrival’s ring and lift would step instead of glide in software.
items.recommend: Let me try a lower frame rate for the lobby only while the board’s first frame is pending, behind a measurement of its frames; you judge the look.

items.title: Proposed, not installed: two small things in shared machinery
items.body:
• .claude/hooks/format.sh formats only some of what the lint checks: client/scripts/*.mjs, client/*.html, bench/*.mjs (E8).
  • Add pytest-timeout: a socket regression in the server tests hangs instead of failing (R8).
items.recommend: Both one-liners; your call since other sessions share them.

items.title: Three silent failures fixed
items.body:
• The computer stalled for ever, saying nothing, if its search chose a move the rules refuse (its board and the engine disagreeing). It now logs the move and plays on (8b968ce).
  • A computer game that outgrew storage rewound to the last copy storage took on a remount or a reload; it now plays on from its latest move, and says so once in the console (5317469).
  • Game ids, the whole credential for an open seat, came from Python’s Mersenne Twister; now from the system’s entropy (26bae12).

items.title: Checks that could pass on broken code, and rules nothing enforced
items.body:
• The computer’s primary row timed a fixed node count: a search made weaker would read faster. It now pins depth, move and the nodes to finish that depth; removing the killer/history updates kept depth and move and now fails on nodes (12,099 → 17,999) (df8083c).
  • The A/B never called a “longest task” row that goes 0 → N ms (a move that starts to hold the page); now it does, and only then (8a020e8, 1aa90ee after review).
  • The server’s “replaced socket” test checked before the disconnect was processed (3016c9b); hudFit passed with nothing measured (e5759d9); the bench’s wait for a pick’s destinations never waited (8311a5b).
  • Lint now stops a board set outside the engine, animation on the browser’s frames or the wall clock, and two ways round the schema and __r3fState rules (a446a69, c023ab5); the build fails if the tutorial’s or a computer game’s page lands in the start page’s bytes (ab48319). Each was planted and seen to fail.
  • One table for the history’s keys, its titles and a new aria-keyshortcuts (f6e8215).

removed.intro: Net +203 lines across client, server and bench (app code +36: the warm-up +18 for links under the entrance and read-backs at rest after −11 for one frame; review/MoveHistory −6; the computer’s fallback +14, storage +8). Nothing deleted outright: pointerEvents.ts (−44, N4′) needs a browser check that competes with timings and was left open; one rejected change (LW, +60) was not kept.

items.title: Linking the lobby’s later programs ahead (LW)
items.body: Two lenses traced 1.75–2.27 s of the joiner’s long tasks to the lobby’s own links after “Join game”. Linked right after the lobby’s first frame, the links left the click → frame window (30 → 25, every pair) but the join’s first frame did not move (+0.4%). The profile shows why: the waits are read-backs behind queued frames, not links. +60 lines for a count; patch kept.

items.title: Smaller
items.body:
• React 19.3: +15.8 KB gz on react-dom, nothing a player waits on faster (measured on the tarballs by a reviewer).
  • Replacing the bench’s PIECE_PIXEL with squarePixel: it rounds to whole pixels and re-casts, which the other does not.

choices.intro:
• Kept the first-pick fix with its trade-off (above) rather than reverting it.
  • Fixed the computer’s fallback to the first legal move, logged, rather than a search without the refused move (R3 open).
  • A refused computer save is logged, not shown (R5, your call).
  • Skipped re-running the whole primary A/B after the last fix (e4ee30c): it changes only when the warm-up draws after the entrance; rechecked on the computer and select sections instead (4 pairs).
  • Merged lenses 1 and 10 into one reviewer; React 19.3 left out (+15.8 KB gz, nothing faster).
  • Kept PIECE_PIXEL in the bench (it rounds to whole pixels; the duplicate does not).

notConfirmed.intro:
• Whether the entrance stutters on a slow real device now that the warm-up links under it: no row measures it (T16), the showcase records on a virtual clock.
  • The full primary A/B on the final commit e4ee30c (it ran on f6e8215; the last fix was rechecked on computer + select only).
  • The move-latency timeouts in the W1b A/B (once per side): not reproduced in the final A/B.
  • N4′ (remove pointerEvents.ts): needs leaving / and /learn at once in a browser; not run.
  • The reviewer’s claims on React 19.3’s size (+15.8 KB gz) were measured by the reviewer on the npm tarballs, not by a build here.

merge.intro: No other sessions were active. Nothing in CLAUDE.md or ARCHITECTURE.md needed changing for this diff (the warm-up’s draw schedule is described only in warm.tsx).

  2. J3: the join’s 5 s is read-backs behind queued lobby frames; try fewer lobby frames while the board starts (a design call).
  3. T16: a row for the entrance’s frame gaps.
  4. R115c: the move list’s follow-scroll forces a layout in every landing (bisect with toggles first).
  5. X5b: H = 0 reopen row and a heap snapshot by constructor; M5/M6 memory trims.
  6. R3/R4: the computer’s fallback move and a stored record that cannot replay.
